facts: Consolidated revenue for full year 2025 was $4.5 billion, down 14% compared to the prior year, while consolidated operating income was $387 million versus $417 million in 2024.
Full year 2025 EPS was $2.78 compared to $3.44 in 2024, and Q4 2025 EPS was a loss of $2.44 versus a loss of $0.93 in Q4 2024.
Global dealer inventory was reduced by 17% year-over-year, meaningfully exceeding the company's stated 10% global reduction target, with North America down 16% and international down 20%.
The company anticipates at least $150 million of annual run rate cost savings impacting 2027 and beyond, on top of previously announced targets, with some savings beginning in the back half of 2026.

For 2026, HDMC is guided to retail and wholesale units of 130,000 to 135,000 each with a one-to-one relationship, while production units are expected to be lower than wholesale, creating operating deleverage.
HDMC 2026 operating income is guided at positive $10 million to a loss of $40 million, HDFS operating income at $45 million to $60 million, and LiveWire operating loss at $70 million to $80 million.
New or increased tariff costs were $67 million in full year 2025, and are forecast at $75 million to $105 million in 2026 based on current tariff levels versus the 2024 baseline.

The HDFS transaction resulted in the sale of approximately $6 billion of retail loan receivables, reducing total gross financing receivables from $7.7 billion to $2 billion, a 74% decline, shifting to a capital-light model.

In full year 2025, the company repurchased $347 million or 13.1 million shares (approximately 11% of shares outstanding), including a $200 million accelerated share repurchase agreement, but plans to be measured on buybacks until the May strategic plan announcement.
North American Q4 retail sales were up 5% year-over-year at 15,847 motorcycles, with sport motorcycle models up 33%, while full year 2025 global retail sales were down 12%.
Q1 fiscal 2026 net sales were $245.8 million (down from $266 million YoY) with adjusted EBITDA of $17.6 million at a 7.2% margin, compared to $27.1 million and 10.2% margin a year ago.

Total comparable sales declined 1.7% in Q1, but would have been +1.2% excluding footwear, which remains a planned H1 headwind expected to flip to a tailwind in H2 as the restructured ~$50 million footwear business returns.
Gross margin compressed 280 bps YoY to 35.3% due to tariffs and planned targeted promotions, while SG&A leveraged 40 bps to 25.9% on store closure savings.
Sub-Brands grew 75% in Q1 and are guided to ~60% growth for full-year 2026, reaching ~$110 million (12% of sales) versus $70 million (7%) in 2025.
The Opening Price Point program scaled to approximately 30% of apparel sales in Q1 at healthy margins, driving double-digit conversion growth and low single-digit growth in units per transaction.
Full-year FY2026 guidance was reaffirmed at net sales of $940–$960 million and adjusted EBITDA of $65–$75 million, implying up to 140 bps of margin expansion versus FY2025.
Q2 guidance calls for sales of $232–$240 million and adjusted EBITDA of $12–$16 million, with continued marketing investment at Q1 levels to support Casting Call.

The store optimization program is substantially complete with 171 total closures (20 in Q1, 7–8 expected in Q2), on track to deliver ~$40 million in FY2026 expense savings ($11 million realized in Q1).
Tariff refunds of $9–$11 million (phase one) and an additional $1.5–$2.5 million (phase two) are anticipated but NOT included in current guidance, providing potential upside.

Guidance assumes tariffs at 10% in H1 stepping up to 15% in H2, with 70% of goods sourced DDP providing protection against freight variability; ended Q1 with $22.8 million cash, $32.8 million drawn on revolver, and $100 million total liquidity.
Aehr reported Q3 fiscal 2026 bookings of $37.2 million with a book-to-bill ratio exceeding 3.5x.

The company's effective backlog (quarter-end backlog plus subsequent bookings) reached a record $50.9 million, with $38.7 million in backlog at quarter-end and $12.2 million in additional bookings in the first 5 weeks of Q4.
Q3 fiscal 2026 revenue was $10.3 million, down 44% year-over-year from $18.3 million, and slightly below consensus.
Non-GAAP net loss for Q3 was $0.05 per diluted share compared to net income of $0.07 per diluted share in Q3 fiscal 2025, though the loss beat consensus by $0.02.

The company fully utilized its $40 million ATM equity program, selling over 1.13 million shares at an average price of $35.38, and ended Q3 with $37.1 million in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash.

Aehr received a $14 million follow-on production order from its lead wafer-level AI accelerator processor customer for multiple fully automated FOX-XP systems for data center training and inference applications.
Full year fiscal 2026 revenue is expected on the high side of $45 million to $50 million, with second half bookings expected on the high side of the $60 million to $80 million range.
The company expects to return to non-GAAP profitability in Q4 fiscal 2026 and expects full year non-GAAP net loss per diluted share between negative $0.13 and negative $0.09.
Aehr's contract manufacturer will begin shipping Sonoma systems this quarter, adding capacity of more than 20 additional Sonoma systems per month to support the anticipated ramp in late summer.

The lead package-level hyperscale customer selected Aehr for production burn-in of their next-generation higher-power AI processor and is forecasting a substantial expansion of Sonoma system purchases beginning in the second half of calendar 2026 and continuing into 2027.
Net sales for Q2 2026 were $118.2 million, representing 9% year-over-year growth and marking the ninth consecutive quarter of year-over-year sales growth.

GAAP operating income was $9.0 million or 7.6% of sales, with adjusted operating income increasing 35% (150 basis points) compared to prior year's adjusted operating income of $6.7 million (6.1% of sales).
Tariff revenue in the quarter was approximately $9.5 million, with unit volumes relatively flat versus the prior quarter on a consolidated basis.
Sales order backlog at quarter end was $82.4 million, which includes estimated tariff surcharges.
The company ended the quarter with a cash balance of $36.8 million, working capital of $126 million, and no bank debt.
New products have consistently contributed 30% to 40% of overall sales over the last 6 to 8 quarters.
The homestyles ready-to-assemble business saw sales decline almost 50% year-over-year.
Current quarter inventory is burdened with approximately 20% tariff levels, and the company expects margin dilution in the second half as cost of sales becomes fully burdened with 25% tariffs.
The company has paused providing forward-looking guidance due to uncertainty regarding both demand and tariff impacts on the business.
The company's strategic account focus encompasses approximately 20 large independent retailers that are progressing their omnichannel capabilities.
DLH reported Q1 fiscal 2026 revenue of $68.9 million versus $90.8 million in the prior year period, a decline of approximately $21.9 million year-over-year.
Approximately $18 million of the quarterly revenue decline was attributable to the conversion of CMOP and Head Start programs to small business set-aside contracts.
Adjusted EBITDA was $6.5 million for Q1 fiscal 2026 compared to $9.9 million in the prior year period, with adjusted EBITDA margin improving sequentially to 9.5%.
Free cash flow usage was approximately $4.8 million in Q1, a significant improvement from $12.1 million of free cash flow used in the prior year first quarter.
Debt stood at $136.6 million at quarter end, increasing during the quarter due to working capital requirements and the impact of the government shutdown.
Management expects to convert approximately 50% to 55% of EBITDA generated during fiscal 2026 to reduce debt by year-end.
The company expects a complete wrap-up of the CMOP program by Q3 of the current fiscal year (fiscal 2026).

The CIO-SP4 contract vehicle has been canceled, causing some pipeline erosion as certain opportunities moved to vehicles where DLH cannot serve as prime contractor, though the majority of opportunities shifted to vehicles where DLH can compete as prime.

The remaining approximately $4 million revenue decline beyond CMOP and Head Start was attributed to government efficiency (DOGE) initiatives and the completion of a USAID international project in January 2025.
DLH reported receiving only one bid opportunity for the entire month of January, described as small, reflecting a continued low volume of new procurement activity despite improved budget visibility.
Total Q3 2025 revenue was $40.2 million, an increase of 12% year-over-year.
The company has already realized $67 million of the targeted $85 million in cost synergies from the Akoya acquisition.
Simoa revenue contributed $23 million with a 36% organic revenue decline, while Spatial reported $17.2 million, down 9% year-over-year.
The company placed 16 Simoa and 27 Spatial instruments in Q3 compared to 13 Simoa instruments in Q3 2024.
U.S. academic revenue declined approximately 30% and pharma revenue declined 23% year-over-year on a pro forma basis.
Full year 2025 revenue guidance is maintained at $130 million to $135 million, implying pro forma revenue of $165 million to $170 million assuming the two companies were combined for the full year.
The company expects to end 2025 with approximately $120 million in cash and no debt, and expects to be cash flow breakeven in 2026.
Diagnostics-related revenue was $2.4 million in the quarter, with LucentAD test receiving a positive pricing recommendation at $897 with final approval expected later this quarter.
Year-to-date R&D investment was approximately $27 million, representing just under 30% of revenue.
Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $11.9 million compared to a loss of $5.5 million in Q3 of the prior year.
Full year 2025 revenue grew 8% year-over-year to $156 million, with over 55% coming from software and services.
Software, services and edge hardware revenue grew 25% year-over-year to $141 million, while battery hardware resale was $15 million for the year.
Year-end ARR grew 16% year-over-year to $61 million, and PowerTrack ARR reached $41 million after adding $7 million in 2025.
Stem achieved its first ever full year positive adjusted EBITDA of $7 million, above the high end of guidance, and first ever positive full year operating cash flow of $7 million.
Full year 2025 cash operating expenses were down 41% from 2024, and fourth quarter cash operating expenses were down 50% year-over-year.
Full year 2025 non-GAAP gross margins reached a record 46%, driven by decreased battery hardware sales and favorable software/service revenue mix.
CARR decreased $3 million sequentially to $67 million due to a managed service customer cancellation that impacted CARR by $3 million, ARR by $1 million, and AUM by 0.1 gigawatt hours.

For 2026, the company guides total revenue of $140 million to $190 million, adjusted EBITDA of $10 million to $15 million (approximately 85% growth at midpoint versus 2025), and ARR of $65 million to $70 million.
The company ended Q4 2025 with $49 million in cash, up from $43 million at the end of Q3 2025, and has sold or written off all DevCo project assets with no further planned DevCo investments.

PowerTrack EMS bookings are expected to begin meaningful revenue conversion at the end of 2026 and into 2027, with utility-scale bookings increasing 10% sequentially in Q4 and nearly all driven by international solar projects.
Lam Research delivered record September quarter revenue of $5.3 billion with gross margin of 50.6% and record operating margin of 35%.
The company's December quarter guidance includes approximately $200 million revenue impact from the recently announced 50% affiliate rule restricting shipments to certain domestic China customers.
Management expects the China export restriction rule to impact calendar year 2026 revenues by approximately $600 million, with China representing less than 30% of overall revenues in 2026.
WFE spending in calendar year 2025 is expected to be slightly better than the prior view of $105 billion, predominantly due to better-than-expected high-bandwidth memory investments.
Management estimates approximately $8 billion of WFE spending for every $100 billion in incremental data center investment.
The company expects over $40 billion in NAND upgrade spending will be required over the next several years as the industry transitions to devices above 200 layers.
China revenue increased to 43% of total revenue in the September quarter, up from 35% in the June quarter, with growth driven by domestic Chinese customers.
December 2025 quarter guidance includes revenue of $5.2 billion, gross margin of 48.5%, operating margin of 33%, and earnings per share of $1.15.

The company allocated approximately $990 million to share buybacks in the September quarter at an average price of approximately $106 per share, and increased the quarterly dividend from $0.23 to $0.26 per share.
Management indicated calendar 2026 WFE looks somewhat second-half weighted and that customer mix will be a headwind to gross margin as China mix normalizes.
Q4 2025 revenue was $43.8 million, a 39% increase year-over-year, while full year 2025 revenue was $159.6 million, up 34% from 2024.
Full year 2025 adjusted EBITDA was $95 million at a 60% margin, yielding a Rule of 40 score of 93.
Q4 2025 net income was $4.3 million, down 63% year-over-year, partly due to $4.6 million of IPO-related expenses incurred during the quarter.
Neptune grew from 23 to 40 capacity partners in 2025, a 74% increase, now supporting 8 programs, and the average commission rate increased 35 basis points year-over-year.
Year-end premium in force was approximately $370 million, reflecting over $90 million of net growth during the year, with full year premium retention of 98%, up 90 basis points year-over-year.
For full year 2026, Neptune raised guidance to approximately $193 million in revenue with an adjusted EBITDA margin between 60% and 61%.

The company refinanced its debt into a $260 million revolving credit facility and ended Q4 with $240 million of total debt outstanding (approximately 2.5x net leverage), subsequently paying down an additional $9 million post-quarter.
Trailing 12-month revenue per employee increased 15% to $2.7 million and adjusted EBITDA per employee increased 14% to $1.6 million for the full year.
Approximately 75% to 80% of Neptune's growth comes from net new flood insurance policies rather than customers switching from the NFIP.
On a go-forward basis, the company expects approximately $6.9 million of RSU-related share-based compensation expense quarterly, and diluted shares outstanding were 149,401,852 at year-end.
Marriott's global portfolio grew 4.7% year-over-year to over 1.75 million rooms across more than 9,700 properties at the end of September.
Third quarter adjusted EBITDA rose 10% to $1.35 billion and adjusted EPS grew 9%, despite global RevPAR increasing only 0.5%.
Marriott Bonvoy membership grew to nearly 260 million members at the end of September, up 18% year-over-year.
Co-branded credit card fees rose 13% in Q3, with international card fees up nearly 20%, driven by strong performance in Japan and UAE.
The pipeline grew to a new high of more than 596,000 rooms at quarter end, with over 250,000 pipeline rooms under construction.
Full year 2025 adjusted EBITDA is expected to increase between 7% and 8% to $5.35 billion to $5.38 billion.
Marriott expects full year capital returns to shareholders to be roughly $4 billion while maintaining leverage in the lower part of the 3 to 3.5x net debt-to-EBITDA range.
Year-to-date room signings in Greater China are up 24% year-over-year through the end of Q3.
Group pace for 2026 is up 7% globally and 8% for U.S., with the 2026 World Cup expected to contribute 30 to 35 basis points to full year global RevPAR growth.
U.S. government transient RevPAR declined 14% year-over-year in Q3, impacting overall business transient performance.
Q1 2026 revenue was $2.3 billion with adjusted EBITDA of $369 million and an adjusted EBITDA margin of 16%, while revenue declined 10% year-over-year and adjusted EPS was $1.22.

Q2 2026 guidance calls for revenue of approximately $2.6 billion to $2.7 billion (slightly below prior year) with an enterprise adjusted EBITDA margin of 20% to 22%, with Roofing expected in the low 30% range, Insulation around 20%, and Doors improving to high single digits.

Free cash flow was a net outflow of $387 million in Q1, reflecting seasonal working capital and $210 million of capital additions, with full-year capex expected around $800 million and D&A approximately $680 million.

The company reaffirmed its commitment to return $1 billion to shareholders in 2026, returned $63 million via dividends in Q1 (no buybacks), and ended the quarter with $1.8 billion in liquidity and a 2.5x debt-to-EBITDA ratio.

Roofing sales fell 14% YoY to $960 million with EBITDA of $231 million at a 24% margin, as the U.S. asphalt shingle market was down approximately 10% and roughly $30 million in carryover curtailment costs hit the quarter (half offset by productivity).

Insulation sales declined 5% to $867 million with adjusted EBITDA of $167 million (down $58 million YoY) at a 19% margin, with management noting industry capacity can support 1.4–1.5 million housing starts.

Doors sales fell 12% to $475 million with EBITDA of $34 million at a 7% margin, including a ~$24 million Q1 revenue headwind from the Q1 distribution divestiture (~$70M annual revenue) and Q4 Oregon components sale (~$50M annual revenue).

Iran-conflict-related inflation is expected to be approximately $60 million in Q2, with about half impacting Roofing and the remainder split between Insulation (more) and Doors, contributing to negative price/cost across segments in Q2.

The company expects to be eligible for approximately $50 million in tariff refunds following a Supreme Court ruling, with $25 million already filed that could benefit Q2, though refunds are excluded from current guidance.

Owens Corning is on track to achieve approximately $135 million in run-rate enterprise cost synergies by midyear (exceeding the $125 million committed) plus an additional $75 million of structural cost improvements, and received ~$280 million in cash proceeds from the glass reinforcements divestiture with another $50–$70 million expected from excess alloy sales.
Q4 net sales rose 9.9% and full-year sales rose 4.3%, with Q4 gross margin expanding to 23.7% from 19.9% a year ago (25.8% excluding noncash and onetime items).
Q4 net income swung to $9.7 million from a $722,000 loss, and full-year net income reached $12.4 million versus a $19.5 million loss the prior year.
FY2027 guidance calls for net sales of $780–$800 million (7.5%–10.2% growth), operating income of $86–$91 million (12.3%–18.8% growth), and EBITDA of $95–$100 million.
Management expects to exit FY2027 at an annualized run rate exceeding $900 million, with more than $100 million of additional annualized sales not yet included in guidance due to timing uncertainty.
New business ramp is weighted to the second half of FY2027 because customers are first working through liquidated inventory from a previous supplier (linked to the First Brands bankruptcy).
Net bank debt was reduced to $80 million against adjusted EBITDA of $86.1 million, yielding a leverage ratio of 0.93x, with total liquidity of approximately $133.7 million.
The company repurchased 955,608 shares for $11.4 million at an average price of $11.88 during FY2026, with $22.1 million remaining under the buyback authorization.

Full-year operating cash flow was $19.2 million, held back by a $32.5 million Q4 accounts receivable build from strong late-March sales and inventory ramp for new business, though three-year cumulative operating cash flow totaled approximately $103.8 million.
A major customer that disrupted Q3 has stabilized, but baseline revenue is now roughly 85% of prior levels after that customer closed about 15% of its stores.

Management is exploring strategic alternatives for the noncore EV emulator business while securing new OE customer commitments, and is relocating heavy-duty operations from Canada to Mexico to improve efficiency.

Qnity delivered full year 2025 net sales of $4.75 billion, representing 10% organic sales growth, and is guiding full year 2026 net sales of $4.97 billion to $5.17 billion (implied midpoint growth of approximately 6.5%).
Full year 2025 adjusted pro forma operating EBITDA was $1.4 billion with a margin of 29.5%, and 2026 EBITDA guidance is $1.465 billion to $1.575 billion.

The company announced a multiyear transformation plan expected to deliver approximately $100 million in EBITDA run rate benefit by the end of 2028, with approximately $140 million in cost to achieve over the next 2 to 3 years.
The Board approved a $500 million share repurchase authorization, and the company ended the year with net leverage of approximately 2.2x versus a long-term target of less than 3x.
The Interconnect Solutions segment grew organic sales 12% in 2025 to $2.1 billion, with advanced packaging, advanced interconnects, and thermal management each growing more than 20% year-over-year.
The Semiconductor Technologies segment delivered net sales of $2.65 billion with 8% organic growth and an adjusted pro forma operating EBITDA margin just above 35%.
Advanced logic and high-bandwidth memory business grew mid-teens in 2025, and advanced packaging solutions represented approximately 10% of total Qnity net sales.

CapEx is expected to elevate to 9% of sales in 2026 (versus a normalized run rate of approximately 6%) to support local-for-local investments and transformation initiatives, resulting in 2026 adjusted free cash flow guidance of $450 million to $550 million versus $706 million generated in 2025.
China accounted for just over 30% of total sales and grew high single digits in 2025, while the rest of Asia and the Americas both grew double digits.
For Q1 2026, the company expects sequential net sales growth of high single digits with a margin profile similar to Q4, and expects ICS to continue outpacing semi segment growth through the year.
Q3 revenue increased 4.5% to $487 million, or 8.4% excluding an $18 million Walden one-week calendar shift that moved revenue into Q2.
Total enrollment grew 6.8%, surpassing 100,000 students and marking the 11th consecutive quarter of total enrollment growth.
Full-year FY2026 revenue guidance was raised to $1.93-$1.945 billion (from $1.9-$1.94 billion) and adjusted EPS guidance to $7.95-$8.15 (from $7.80-$8.00), implying 19-22% EPS growth.
Chamberlain returned to positive total enrollment growth ahead of plan at +0.5% to 40,767 students, with management expecting a similar growth rate in Q4.
Walden enrollment grew 12.3% to a record 54,474 students, with adjusted EBITDA margin (ex-calendar shift) of 33.1%, up 280 basis points year-over-year.
Medical and Veterinary segment revenue rose 8.9% to $103.5 million and adjusted EBITDA grew 20.1% to $27.5 million, with margin expanding 250 basis points to 26.5%.
Consolidated adjusted EBITDA was $127.9 million, or $145.9 million (+14.2%, 28.9% margin, +150 bps) excluding the Walden timing impact.
Trailing 12-month free cash flow grew 17% to $336 million, net leverage declined to 0.7x, and the company repurchased $66 million of stock in the quarter.
The company refinanced into a $510 million Term Loan B, cutting 50 basis points off its rate and extending maturity to 2033.

Six new Chamberlain campuses are in active development with the first beginning teaching in September, and CapEx is expected to step up further in Q4 from $20 million in Q3 and $31 million in the first half.
Adeia delivered record full-year 2025 revenue of $443 million, exceeding the upper end of revised guidance, with operating income of $276 million and adjusted EBITDA of $278 million.
Fourth quarter 2025 revenue was a record $182.6 million, driven by 9 deals including 4 new customers, with non-Pay-TV recurring revenue growing 30% year-over-year.

Full-year 2026 revenue guidance is $395 million to $435 million, with an expected adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 55%, down from 2025 levels primarily due to a projected $5 million to $10 million increase in litigation expense above the $25 million spent in 2025.

Pay-TV is expected to decline to approximately 35% to 40% of forecasted 2026 revenue, down from a historical average of approximately 50% to 60%, while OTT is expected to represent approximately 30% to 35% of total revenue.
Since 2022, non-Pay-TV recurring revenue has grown by more than 60%, and in 2025 alone it grew by more than 20%.

Semiconductor revenue grew approximately 40% year-over-year, from about $18 million in 2024 to about $26 million in 2025, representing roughly 6% of total revenue with media comprising approximately 94%.

Adeia signed a multiyear license agreement with Microsoft in early 2026 covering its media portfolio with broad applicability to Microsoft's consumer electronics and social media products and services.

The company reduced debt by $60 million in 2025, ending Q4 with a term loan balance of $426.7 million and cash/equivalents/marketable securities of $136.7 million, with an effective interest rate of 7.5%.
Adeia added a record 12 new customers in 2025 across 26 total license agreements, and the company's OTT market share currently stands at approximately 50%.

DIRECTV has filed litigation challenging the need for a new license agreement, to which Adeia has responded with a breach of contract suit, while the company maintains that the vast majority of U.S. Pay-TV operators are licensed with several agreements extending into the next decade.
Q3 revenue grew 14% year-over-year to $1.172 billion, with organic revenue growth of 11% and adjusted EPS of $5.70 per share.
Q4 guidance was revised up to revenue of $1.235 billion and cash EPS of $5.90 at the midpoint, with organic revenue growth expected at approximately 10%.
Full year 2025 is expected to finish above $4.5 billion in revenue (up 14%) and above $21 in cash EPS, higher than the initial February profit guidance.
Corporate Payments segment grew 17% organically in Q3 despite a 100 basis point drag from float revenue compression, with spend volumes increasing 57% on a reported basis to over $68 billion.
U.S. Vehicle Payments organic revenue growth improved 500 basis points sequentially to 5%, with the overall Vehicle Payments segment reaching 10% organic growth.
New sales bookings grew 24% in Q3, with retention improving to 92.4%.
The company expects at least $0.75 of incremental accretion in 2026 from the combined Alpha and Avid acquisitions.
Alpha acquisition closed October 31 and is expected to add approximately $55 million in revenue in Q4 2025.
The company is marketing two divestitures hoping to fetch up to $1.5 billion, with first bids due in the coming weeks.
Leverage ended Q3 at 2.4x with $3.5 billion in liquidity, and the company repurchased approximately 600,000 shares for $192 million, with about $1 billion authorized for future repurchases.

Since inception, Innventure has deployed approximately $160 million of balance sheet capital into its operating companies, generating roughly $860 million in net asset value, including approximately $460 million distributed directly to shareholders through PureCycle.
In the first quarter of 2026 alone, Accelsius generated more than $50 million in contracted backlog, all tied to greenfield next-generation data center developments.
Accelsius is expected to exit December 2026 with positive operating cash flow, implying an annual revenue run rate of approximately $100 million.
In December 2025, Accelsius closed the second tranche of a $65 million Series B investment led by Johnson Controls and Legrand, valuing the company at approximately $665 million post-money.
Consolidated G&A declined from $29.7 million in Q4 2024 to $11.5 million in Q4 2025, a 61% reduction, with G&A decreasing sequentially every quarter since Innventure went public.
Innventure's consolidated 2025 revenue was $2.1 million, up from $1.2 million in 2024, with Accelsius revenue increasing from $0.3 million in 2024 to $1.6 million in 2025.

On a consolidated basis, Innventure ended 2025 with $65.4 million of cash, restricted cash and cash equivalents, up from $11.1 million at the end of 2024, and raised an additional $40 million in a January 2026 registered direct offering.
Excluding the $347 million noncash goodwill adjustment and other minor noncash items, adjusted EBITDA for 2025 was a loss of $78.8 million.

AeroFlexx's near-term commercial pipeline stands at approximately $30 million, including roughly one-third in final negotiations, with 6 consecutive quarters of revenue delivered across multiple end markets.

Innventure expects to reach consolidated cash flow positivity in 2028, driven by Accelsius expecting to achieve cash flow positivity this year and the board composition transitioning from 5 independent and 4 executive directors to a target of 7 independent and 2 executive directors by June.

Q1 2026 net sales of $1.7 billion were up 4% year-over-year on 2% organic growth and a 2% currency benefit, with operating EBITDA of $414 million up 15% and margins expanding 230 basis points to 24.6% (130 bps on a pro-forma basis).

Adjusted EPS of $0.55 increased 53% year-over-year on a reported basis and 20% on a pro-forma basis, driven by $0.06 from higher segment earnings and $0.03 from a lower tax rate, lower share count and FX.

DuPont raised full-year 2026 guidance to net sales of about $7.185 billion (+$80 million vs. prior), operating EBITDA of about $1.745 billion, and adjusted EPS of $2.35–$2.40 (a $0.10 increase), now assuming ~4% organic growth including ~1% from pricing actions.

The company announced a $275 million accelerated share repurchase under its existing $2 billion program, on top of a previously completed $500 million ASR, following $1.1 billion in net proceeds from the April 1 Aramids divestiture.

Middle East conflict caused $10 million of Water sales to be unable to ship in Q1, and total Middle East exposure is approximately $300 million (~4% of revenue), split evenly between sales into and sourcing from the region.

Management expects ~$90 million of incremental input costs from the Middle East conflict to be fully offset by surcharges and price increases (mostly effective May 1), with ~$25 million of price on the top line in Q2 creating a ~30 bps margin headwind sequentially.

Healthcare & Water Technologies Q1 sales of $806 million grew 6% (3% organic) with EBITDA margins expanding 110 bps to 30.3%; healthcare grew high single digits organically while water declined low-to-mid single digits due to Middle East disruptions.

Diversified Industrials Q1 sales of $875 million were up 3% (organic flat) with EBITDA margins expanding 110 bps to 22.9%, as building technologies declined low single digits on construction weakness while industrial technologies grew low single digits.

Q2 2026 guidance calls for net sales of ~$1.8 billion (~3% organic growth), operating EBITDA of ~$430 million and adjusted EPS of $0.59, with first-half results representing ~48% of full-year guidance at the midpoint.

Transaction-adjusted free cash flow was $147 million in Q1 with 65% conversion, and management reaffirmed full-year free cash flow conversion of greater than 90%; stranded cost removal is on track with ~$10 million expected out this year toward a $30 million target over two years.
Q1 FY2026 net income was $22.5 million with diluted EPS of $2.67, ROE of 17.64%, and ROA of 2.13%.
Tangible book value reached $59.98 per share, just under $60.

Loan purchases totaled $152.7 million UPB at an invested amount of $144.6 million (purchase price just under $0.95), representing the second largest purchase quarter in 3 years excluding two large transactions.
Net interest margin compressed to 4.59% from 5.1% in the prior quarter, with pre-provision net interest income declining from $59.4 million to $48.2 million.
SBA gain on sale decreased from $8.2 million to $4.1 million quarter-over-quarter, reducing diluted EPS by $0.34.
Average loan balances declined $92 million from the linked quarter because most purchases and originations occurred late in September.
The bank has $207 million of discount on its purchased loan book that can be recognized as transactional income upon payoffs.
The new insured small business loan product launched October 1 has closed approximately $10 million since inception.
Loan originations totaled $134 million comprising 22 loans with average balance of $6 million, LTVs just over 50%, and average interest rate just under 8%.
The effective tax rate is expected to be 31% to 32% for the remainder of fiscal year 2026.
Principal Financial delivered 13% adjusted earnings per share growth year-over-year and 14% year-to-date, above the company's target range.
The company returned $400 million of capital to shareholders in Q3 2025, including $225 million in share repurchases and $173 million in common stock dividends.
Total company managed AUM reached $784 billion, increasing 4% sequentially, driven by strong market performance and positive net cash flow of $400 million.
The company has $1.6 billion of excess and available capital, which is $150 million higher than at the start of Q3, with an estimated risk-based capital ratio of 400%.
